subject: ImageRename mixes up photos while having multiple cameras per station

messages.author: 398291f1faced554
messages.subject: ImageRename mixes up photos while having multiple cameras per station
parts:
Hello,

While using imageRename, CamtrapR is  mixing up photos between cameras at a station.  It can clearly be seen from the renaming table that it is not picking up the correct camera according to the directory .  I have attached the renaming table. The first 3 lines itself show that although the camera should be BH5-A according to the directory, it selects the camera as BH3-A and renames the file accordingly.  This is the directory structure I used

Station Camera
Bela BH3-A

BH5-A

CB3-A

CB4-A
Nag BH5-C

CB3-C

CB4-C
Saucer02 ML1


Some are correctly piicked up, some are wrong. The total number of images in each directory is preserved. The images themselves are mixed up. I have used cameras of 3 different makes here. Could that be causing an issue? Any help is greatly appreciated. 

Regards,
Tara

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: ImageRename mixes up photos while having multiple cameras per station
parts:
Hi Tara,
can you share your code please? 
The problem may have to do with the double underscores ("__") in some file names. camtrapR uses double underscores to separate station, camera IDs etc in the newly created file names. These are then used to copy files. 
Can you try renaming all those images and rerun the function? Software like Bulk Rename Utility makes that task easier.
Thank you,
Jürgen

messages.author: 398291f1faced554
messages.subject: Re: ImageRename mixes up photos while having multiple cameras per station
parts:
Hi Jurgen,

I use 3 types of cameras, Cuddeback (CB) Bushnell(BH) and moultrie (ML). Only  CB uses double underscores to name it's images. I created a test case scenario ( which I am attaching here ) with 2 stations with 2 cameras each. Station Belachapar has 2 CB cams and station Nagbehra has 1 CB and 1 ML cam. Belachapar is correctly renamed and Nagbehra is not , so it does seem that this issue only pops up when you have  cameras of different make at a station.

I will try renaming in bulk and see if that solves the issue. Thank you very much for the suggestion.
